Principal neighborhood aggregation (PNA)

Source: R/propagation-layers.R
pna_conv.Rd

The PNA layer of Corso, Cavalleri, Beaini, Liò and Veličković (2020), in the single tower form of PyTorch Geometric's PNAConv (one pre and one post layer, divide_input = FALSE). For node \(i\) with in degree \(d_i\):

Usage

pna_conv(
  in_features,
  out_features,
  deg,
  aggregators = c("mean", "min", "max", "std"),
  scalers = c("identity", "amplification", "attenuation"),
  edge_dim = NULL
)

pna_degree(graphs)

Arguments

in_features, out_features

Feature sizes.

deg

Degree histogram from pna_degree().

aggregators

Any of "mean", "min", "max", "std", "sum".

scalers

Any of "identity", "amplification", "attenuation", "linear", "inverse_linear".

edge_dim

Edge feature size, or NULL.

graphs

A graph_data object or a list of them.

Value

pna_conv(): an nn_module called as layer(x, edge_index, edge_attr = NULL). pna_degree(): an integer vector.

Details

  1. messages \(m_{ji} = U [x_i \Vert x_j \Vert E e_{ji}]\) (the edge term only with edge_dim);

  2. each aggregator (mean, min, max, std, sum) is applied to the incoming messages and each result is multiplied by each scaler: identity, amplification \(\log(d_i + 1) / \delta\), attenuation \(\delta / \log(d_i + 1)\), linear \(d_i / \bar d\) or inverse linear \(\bar d / d_i\), with \(d_i\) clamped to at least 1 and \(\delta\), \(\bar d\) the mean of \(\log(d + 1)\) and of \(d\) over the training degree histogram deg;

  3. \(x_i' = W_2 \, M [x_i \Vert \text{scaled aggregates}]\).

The std aggregator is \(\sqrt{\max(\mathrm{var}, 0) + 10^{-5}}\), so nodes without incoming edges, or with identical incoming messages, get \(\sqrt{10^{-5}}\) from it and zeros from every other aggregator. Other implementations may treat zero variance differently.

pna_degree() computes the in degree histogram deg from training graphs: element \(d + 1\) counts nodes with in degree \(d\).

Input x is N by F; output N by F'. No self loops are added; edge input is edge_attr when edge_dim is set. Cost: \(O(E F^2)\) for the message transform, \(O(a E F)\) for a aggregators, and \(O(N a s F F')\) for the post transform with s scalers; memory holds E by F messages and the N by \((a s + 1) F\) concatenation.

The benchmark workflow (benchmarks/pyg/) copies the weights of a layer with the mean, min, max and sum aggregators and all five scalers, and of one with the std aggregator, into PyTorch Geometric's PNAConv (one tower, one pre and post layer) and checks that the outputs agree (the first agreed to 2e-6 on CI).

References

Corso, Cavalleri, Beaini, Liò and Veličković (2020) Principal neighbourhood aggregation for graph nets.

Examples

if (torch::torch_is_installed()) {
  g <- dataset_karate()
  tt <- graph_tensors(g)
  layer <- pna_conv(34, 8, deg = pna_degree(g))
  layer(tt$x, tt$edge_index)$shape
}
#> [1] 34  8
